Messages.Author: Totengräber
Messages.Body:
Quick question, to which I think I know the answer:

Reverend Balckwood strikes with Theft of Vitae, what happens?

1) 3 blood is stolen
2) 2 blood is stolen and 1 normal damage is taken
3) 2 blood is stolen

Relavent card texts:
Reverend Blackwood [Sabbat]
Cardtype: Vampire
Clan: Tremere antitribu
Capacity: 6
Discipline: THA DOM obf
Sabbat Bishop: Reverend Blackwood inflicts +1 damage with any strike
card that requires Thaumaturgy.

Theft of Vitae [Jyhad, V:TES, Sabbat]
Cardtype: Combat
Discipline: Thaumaturgy
[tha] Strike: steal 1 blood. Usable at long range.
[THA] Strike: steal 2 blood. Usable at long range.

Relavant rules references:
[6.4.5] Steal Blood: ... This does not count as damage ...

I think the answer is #3, but I just need confirmation.

Later,
Todd Dunn
V:EKN Prince of Noblesville, IN

<zombi...@aol.com> writes

>>Why?? 0+1 = 1 .....
>
>It's not "zero" damage. There is no damage there at all to modify. >>
>

Sloppiness of card text is one possibility.

They could be following the standard notion that you cannot modify
something that isn't there, also. (e.g. you cannot, as some players
have tried, play Bonding on a political action at superior for the
stealth - since there is no bleed there to modify).

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <20010731041132...@ng-fz1.aol.com>, ZombieCreep
<zombi...@aol.com> writes

>but why cant you add damage to a non damage strike?.... i dont want to hear
>"cuz its in the rules" i want a reason

Because it's in the rules.

The standard template is that you cannot add to something that isn't
there.

"Adding damage to strikes which are not damage dealing strikes will not
deal damage (e.g., using Lucky Blow and choosing your Rowan Ring melee
weapon won't deal damage) [RTR 19960221] "

The standard template affects Theft just as much as Rowan Ring.


